claim: Traditional extracellular recordings have been powerful and scalable.
source: Traditional extracellular recordings have been powerful and scalable, but much less is known about the intracellular processes that lead to spiking activity.
evidence: This is a statement about the established capabilities of extracellular recording methods in neuroscience.

claim: Much less is known about the intracellular processes that lead to spiking activity compared to extracellular recordings.
source: Traditional extracellular recordings have been powerful and scalable, but much less is known about the intracellular processes that lead to spiking activity.
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The multipatcher is capable of automatically obtaining blind whole-cell patch clamp recordings from multiple neurons simultaneously.
source: We present a robotic system, the multipatcher, capable of automatically obtaining blind whole-cell patch clamp recordings from multiple neurons simultaneously.
evidence: This is the primary claim about the capability of the developed system, supported by experimental demonstrations throughout the paper.

claim: The multipatcher significantly extends automated patch clamping to guide four interacting electrodes in a coordinated fashion.
source: The multipatcher significantly extends automated patch clamping, or 'autopatching', to guide four interacting electrodes in a coordinated fashion, avoiding mechanical coupling in the brain.
evidence: This describes the technical advancement of the system, demonstrated through the experimental results.

claim: The multipatcher avoids mechanical coupling in the brain.
source: The multipatcher significantly extends automated patch clamping, or 'autopatching', to guide four interacting electrodes in a coordinated fashion, avoiding mechanical coupling in the brain.
evidence: This is a design goal achieved through the interaction algorithm, as demonstrated by the successful recordings.

claim: A multipatcher with four electrodes took an average of 10 min to obtain dual or triple recordings.
source: A multipatcher with four electrodes took an average of 10 min to obtain dual or triple recordings in 29% of trials in anesthetized mice, and in 18% of the trials in awake mice, thus illustrating practical yield and throughput to obtain multiple, simultaneous whole-cell recordings in vivo.
evidence: This is a quantitative measurement of system performance reported in the results.

claim: The multipatcher obtained dual or triple recordings in 29% of trials in anesthetized mice.
source: A multipatcher with four electrodes took an average of 10 min to obtain dual or triple recordings in 29% of trials in anesthetized mice, and in 18% of the trials in awake mice, thus illustrating practical yield and throughput to obtain multiple, simultaneous whole-cell recordings in vivo.
evidence: This is a quantitative success rate measured experimentally.

claim: The multipatcher obtained dual or triple recordings in 18% of trials in awake mice.
source: A multipatcher with four electrodes took an average of 10 min to obtain dual or triple recordings in 29% of trials in anesthetized mice, and in 18% of the trials in awake mice, thus illustrating practical yield and throughput to obtain multiple, simultaneous whole-cell recordings in vivo.
evidence: This is a quantitative success rate measured experimentally in awake animals.

claim: Mammalian brains consist of neurons organized into densely interconnected circuits.
source: Mammalian brains consist of neurons organized into densely interconnected circuits.
evidence: This is established knowledge about brain organization.

claim: Circuit-level characterization of neuronal activities has traditionally been carried out using extracellular recording probes.
source: Traditionally circuit-level characterization of neuronal activities has been carried out using extracellular recording probes (Buzsáki, 2004) or using genetically encoded calcium indicators (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work in the field.

claim: Circuit-level characterization of neuronal activities has traditionally been carried out using genetically encoded calcium indicators.
source: Traditionally circuit-level characterization of neuronal activities has been carried out using extracellular recording probes (Buzsáki, 2004) or using genetically encoded calcium indicators (Chen et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Extracellular recording probes and genetically encoded calcium indicators reveal supra-threshold spiking activities of individual neurons in a circuit.
source: While these methods reveal supra-threshold spiking activities of individual neurons in a circuit, they cannot examine synaptic and subthreshold events in neurons, important for understanding the processes within and between cells that lead to spiking.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of these methods based on established knowledge.

claim: Extracellular recording probes and genetically encoded calcium indicators cannot examine synaptic and subthreshold events in neurons.
source: While these methods reveal supra-threshold spiking activities of individual neurons in a circuit, they cannot examine synaptic and subthreshold events in neurons, important for understanding the processes within and between cells that lead to spiking.
evidence: This describes the limitations of these methods based on established knowledge.

claim: Synaptic and subthreshold events in neurons are important for understanding the processes within and between cells that lead to spiking.
source: While these methods reveal supra-threshold spiking activities of individual neurons in a circuit, they cannot examine synaptic and subthreshold events in neurons, important for understanding the processes within and between cells that lead to spiking.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the importance of subthreshold events in neuroscience.

claim: A few studies have performed simultaneous multi-neuron intracellular recordings in vivo.
source: While a few studies have performed simultaneous multi-neuron intracellular recordings in vivo (van Welie et al., 2016; Jouhanneau et al., 2015; Poulet and Petersen, 2008), the difficulty of the technique limits its use.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: The difficulty of simultaneous multi-neuron intracellular recording technique limits its use.
source: While a few studies have performed simultaneous multi-neuron intracellular recordings in vivo (van Welie et al., 2016; Jouhanneau et al., 2015; Poulet and Petersen, 2008), the difficulty of the technique limits its use.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limited number of studies performing this technique.

claim: The autopatcher performs fully-automated whole-cell patch clamping of single neurons in the living mouse brain.
source: Recently we developed a robot, called the 'autopatcher', that performs fully-automated whole-cell patch clamping of single neurons in the living mouse brain (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: The autopatcher uses pipette impedance measurements to hunt for neurons.
source: The autopatcher uses pipette impedance measurements to hunt for neurons, followed by gigasealing and break-in using electronically controlled pressure regulators.
evidence: This describes the technical approach of the autopatcher system.

claim: The autopatcher performs gigasealing and break-in using electronically controlled pressure regulators.
source: The autopatcher uses pipette impedance measurements to hunt for neurons, followed by gigasealing and break-in using electronically controlled pressure regulators.
evidence: This describes the technical approach of the autopatcher system.

claim: Several straightforward attempts to scale up the autopatcher approach to achieve multi-neuron recordings exhibited very low yield.
source: We explored several straightforward attempts to scale up this approach to achieve multi-neuron recordings, but they exhibited very low yield.
evidence: This is based on pilot studies conducted by the authors.

claim: Robots engaged in stationary activities, such as gigasealing, would be disrupted by robots engaged in motion, such as during neuron hunting.
source: From these pilot studies, we hypothesized that robots engaged in stationary activities, such as the delicate task of gigasealing, would be disrupted by robots engaged in motion, such as during the task of neuron hunting.
evidence: This is a hypothesis derived from observations in pilot studies.

claim: An optimal combination of hardware and software should optimize the interaction between stationary and active tasks across pipettes.
source: Therefore, an optimal combination of hardware and software should optimize the interaction between stationary and active tasks across pipettes.
evidence: This is a design principle inferred from the hypothesis about robot interactions.

claim: The multipatcher robot obtained dual or triple whole-cell recordings in 29% of trials under anesthetized conditions.
source: Under anesthetized conditions, the multipatcher robot obtained dual or triple whole-cell recordings in 29% of trials, and at least one whole-cell recording in 90% of trials.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments.

claim: The multipatcher robot obtained at least one whole-cell recording in 90% of trials under anesthetized conditions.
source: Under anesthetized conditions, the multipatcher robot obtained dual or triple whole-cell recordings in 29% of trials, and at least one whole-cell recording in 90% of trials.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments.

claim: An individual robot had the same whole-cell yield when used in the multipatcher robot as it did when working alone (31%).
source: An individual robot had the same whole-cell yield when used in our multipatcher robot as it did when working alone (31%).
evidence: This is a comparison of yields showing that the multipatcher does not reduce individual pipette performance.

claim: In awake mice the multipatcher obtained dual or triple whole-cell recordings in 18% of the trials.
source: In awake mice the multipatcher obtained dual or triple whole-cell recordings in 18% of the trials.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments in awake animals.

claim: The multipatcher is a practical solution for performing intracellular recordings from multiple neurons in the intact brain.
source: Thus, the multipatcher is a practical solution for performing intracellular recordings from multiple neurons in the intact brain.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the demonstrated performance metrics.

claim: The multipatcher robot was built by extending some of the hardware components of the previously described autopatcher robot.
source: The multipatcher robot was built by extending some of the hardware components of our previously described autopatcher robot (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the development approach, referencing prior work.

claim: The multipatcher consists of an array of four robotic arms for manipulating the patch recording pipettes.
source: It consists of an array of four robotic arms for manipulating the patch recording pipettes, patch amplifiers, a signal control box, a computer with an interface board, and a pressure control box (Figure 1, Figure 1—figure supplements 1 and 2, and Supplementary files 1, 2 and 3).
evidence: This is a description of the hardware components, supported by figures.

claim: The internal pressures of the patch pipettes were independently controlled using the pressure control box.
source: The internal pressures of the patch pipettes were independently controlled using the pressure control box (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes a key hardware capability shown in the figure.

claim: The pipettes that reached neurons last and attempted to establish gigaseal immediately successfully formed gigaseals 36.8% of the time (7/19 pipettes) in the first algorithm iteration.
source: The pipettes reaching neurons last, and thereby attempting to establish gigaseal immediately, successfully formed gigaseals 36.8% of the time (7/19 pipettes).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from testing the first algorithm iteration.

claim: In the first algorithm iteration, successful gigaseals were formed 16.3% of the time (8/49 pipettes) in the rest of attempts where pipettes had to wait.
source: In the rest of attempts, successful gigaseals were formed 16.3% of the time (8/49 pipettes).
evidence: This is a quantitative result showing reduced success rate for waiting pipettes.

claim: Waiting significantly lowered gigaseal yield relative to both not waiting and previously reported gigaseal yields.
source: Thus waiting significantly lowered gigaseal yield relative to both not waiting and previously reported gigaseal yields (van Welie et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a comparative conclusion drawn from the data and cited prior work.

claim: Tissue displacements caused by either motion of other pipettes in the brain or the force of the ejected intracellular pipette solution was large enough to dislodge neurons.
source: This indicates that tissue displacements, caused perhaps by either motion of other pipettes in the brain or the force of the ejected intracellular pipette solution, was large enough to dislodge neurons.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that resistance fell back to baseline in waiting pipettes.

claim: Only 20.5% (8 out of 39 pipettes) established successful gigaseals even when elevated resistance readings indicating proximity to a neuron were observed.
source: Further, only 20.5%, 8 out of the remaining 39 pipettes, established successful gigaseals, even when elevated resistance readings, indicating proximity to a neuron, were observed.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the first algorithm iteration.

claim: Constant exposure to the intracellular pipette solution while waiting possibly had a deleterious effect on the neurons, resulting in lower rates of gigasealing.
source: We hypothesized that the constant exposure to the intracellular pipette solution while waiting possibly had a deleterious effect on the neurons, resulting in lower rates of gigasealing.
evidence: This is a hypothesis proposed to explain the observed low gigaseal rates.

claim: The movement of pipette actuator arms during neuron hunting resulted in electrical noise.
source: Other issues encountered during this strategy were that the movement of pipette actuator arms during neuron hunting resulted in electrical noise, and when coincident with the resistance measurements in other channels, resulted in spurious readings.
evidence: This is an observation from testing the first algorithm iteration.

claim: Movement of pipette actuator arms during neuron hunting when coincident with resistance measurements in other channels resulted in spurious readings.
source: Other issues encountered during this strategy were that the movement of pipette actuator arms during neuron hunting resulted in electrical noise, and when coincident with the resistance measurements in other channels, resulted in spurious readings.
evidence: This is an observation from testing the first algorithm iteration.

claim: Once either the gigasealed cell attached or whole-cell stage has been achieved, the configuration is remarkably stable against motion artifacts.
source: As it has been observed previously, once either the gigasealed cell attached or whole-cell stage has been achieved, the configuration is remarkably stable against motion artifacts.
evidence: This is established knowledge from prior observations in the field.

claim: It is possible to record in the whole-cell state from head-fixed rodents.
source: This has been used previously to record in the whole-cell state from head-fixed rodents (Poulet and Petersen, 2008; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016; Chabrol et al., 2015; Margrie et al., 2002; Margrie et al., 2003) and freely moving animals (Epsztein et al., 2010; Lee et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to prior work.

claim: It is possible to record in the whole-cell state from freely moving animals.
source: This has been used previously to record in the whole-cell state from head-fixed rodents (Poulet and Petersen, 2008; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012; Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016; Chabrol et al., 2015; Margrie et al., 2002; Margrie et al., 2003) and freely moving animals (Epsztein et al., 2010; Lee et al., 2009; Lee et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: It is possible to carry out loose cell attached recordings for tens of minutes to hours.
source: Several groups have also shown that it is possible to carry out loose cell attached recordings for tens of minutes to hours (DeWeese et al., 2003; Tang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Using the third and final algorithm, successful gigasealed cell attached states were obtained in 58% of the active pipettes (77 out of 133 pipettes in 41 trials).
source: Using this algorithm, we were able to get successful gigasealed cell attached states in 58% of the active pipettes (77 out of 133 pipettes in 41 trials, 41 pipettes were deactivated at the end of the initial localization step due to blockage or clogging).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from testing the final algorithm.

claim: The gigasealing success rate of 58% with the final algorithm was the highest yield obtained from all three iterations.
source: This was the highest yield we obtained from all three iterations, and exceeded the gigasealing success rate that we obtained with our autopatcher algorithm (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparative statement about the performance of different algorithm iterations.

claim: The gigasealing success rate of 58% with the final algorithm exceeded the gigasealing success rate obtained with the autopatcher algorithm.
source: This was the highest yield we obtained from all three iterations, and exceeded the gigasealing success rate that we obtained with our autopatcher algorithm (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison with prior work showing improvement.

claim: Nineteen percent of the pipette tips were blocked or fouled in the initial descent to depth (31/164 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice).
source: Nineteen percent of the pipette tips were blocked or fouled in the initial descent to depth (31/164 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice), comparable to that obtained previously (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments in anesthetized animals.

claim: The 19% blockage rate was comparable to that obtained previously with the autopatcher.
source: Nineteen percent of the pipette tips were blocked or fouled in the initial descent to depth (31/164 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice), comparable to that obtained previously (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison with prior work showing consistency.

claim: Of the pipettes that executed neuron hunting, 57% (77/133 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice) established successful gigaseals.
source: Of the pipettes that executed neuron hunting, 57% (77/133 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice) established successful gigaseals, of which 67.5% (52/77 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice) yielded successful whole-cell recordings of necessary quality.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments in anesthetized animals.

claim: Of the gigasealed pipettes, 67.5% (52/77 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice) yielded successful whole-cell recordings of necessary quality.
source: Of the pipettes that executed neuron hunting, 57% (77/133 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice) established successful gigaseals, of which 67.5% (52/77 pipettes in 41 trials, eight mice) yielded successful whole-cell recordings of necessary quality.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments in anesthetized animals.

claim: Overall, each pipette had a 31.7% (52/164 pipettes) chance of establishing a whole-cell recording.
source: Overall, each pipette had a 31.7% (52/164 pipettes) chance of establishing a whole-cell recording.
evidence: This is a calculated overall success rate from the experimental data.

claim: The high percentage of gigaseals obtained can be attributed to improvements made in surgical procedures, for example using an autodrilling robot to perform craniotomies.
source: We hypothesize that the high percentage of gigaseals obtained can be attributed to improvements made in our surgical procedures, for example using an autodrilling robot (Pak et al., 2015) to perform craniotomies.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the reason for improved performance, referencing a technical improvement.

claim: A decrease in break-in success rate was observed as compared to the previous autopatcher study.
source: We did observe a decrease in break-in success rate as compared to our previous study (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a comparison with prior work showing a difference in performance.

claim: Of the 77 neurons that were gigasealed, successful whole-cell recordings were established in 52 neurons, achieving a break-in success rate of 67.5%.
source: Of the 77 neurons that were gigasealed, we established successful whole-cell recordings in 52 neurons, achieving a break-in success rate of 67.5%.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments.

claim: A small fraction (6.4%, 5/77 gigasealed neurons in 41 trials, eight mice) lost gigaseal attachment to the neurons while waiting for break-in.
source: A small fraction (6.4%, 5/77 gigasealed neurons in 41 trials, eight mice) lost gigaseal attachment to the neurons while waiting.
evidence: This is a quantitative observation about a failure mode.

claim: The increased duration of holding at the gigaseal stage may have made break-in more difficult.
source: It is also possible that, of the ones that remained gigasealed, the increased duration of holding at this stage made break-in more difficult, although we did not systematically explore this.
evidence: This is speculation about a potential cause of reduced break-in success.

claim: The multipatcher attempted a total of 97 multipatching trials (with 97 × 4 = 388 pipettes) in 32 awake, head restrained mice.
source: We attempted a total of 97 multipatching trials (with 97 × 4 = 388 pipettes) in 32 awake, head restrained mice, which yielded 70 successful whole-cell recordings that matched the quality criterion (Figure 5c and d, and Figure 5—source data 5–7).
evidence: This is a quantitative description of the experimental effort in awake animals.

claim: The multipatcher yielded 70 successful whole-cell recordings that matched the quality criterion in awake mice.
source: We attempted a total of 97 multipatching trials (with 97 × 4 = 388 pipettes) in 32 awake, head restrained mice, which yielded 70 successful whole-cell recordings that matched the quality criterion (Figure 5c and d, and Figure 5—source data 5–7).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments in awake animals.

claim: If each pipette was considered individually in awake mice, it had a 17.3% chance of obtaining a whole-cell patch recording (67/388 pipettes).
source: Thus, if each pipette was considered individually, it had an 17.3% chance of obtaining a whole-cell patch recording (67/388 pipettes).
evidence: This is a calculated success rate from the experimental data in awake animals.

claim: In 44.3% (43/97) of the trials in awake mice, no usable whole-cell patch recordings were obtained.
source: In 44.3% (43/97) of the trials, no usable whole-cell patch recordings were obtained, perhaps due to additional motion of the brain as compared to anesthetized mice.
evidence: This is a quantitative result showing the failure rate in awake animals.

claim: The failure to obtain recordings in 44.3% of trials in awake mice was perhaps due to additional motion of the brain as compared to anesthetized mice.
source: In 44.3% (43/97) of the trials, no usable whole-cell patch recordings were obtained, perhaps due to additional motion of the brain as compared to anesthetized mice.
evidence: This is speculation about the cause of failures in awake animals.

claim: At least one whole-cell patch clamp recording was obtained in 55.7% (54/97) of trials in awake mice.
source: At least one whole-cell patch clamp recording was obtained in 55.7% (54/97) of trials, with 17.5% (17/97) of the trials resulting in dual or triple whole-cell patch clamp recordings.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments in awake animals.

claim: 17.5% (17/97) of the trials in awake mice resulted in dual or triple whole-cell patch clamp recordings.
source: At least one whole-cell patch clamp recording was obtained in 55.7% (54/97) of trials, with 17.5% (17/97) of the trials resulting in dual or triple whole-cell patch clamp recordings.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from experiments in awake animals.

claim: Approximately half (48.6%) of recordings obtained in awake head-fixed animals (34/70 neurons, 32 mice) were obtained in experiments involving injection of anesthetics.
source: Approximately half (48.6%) of recordings obtained in awake head-fixed animals (34/70 neurons, 32 mice), such as those shown in Figure 5a and b, were obtained in experiments involving injection of anesthetics for a separate study (data unpublished).
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions for a subset of recordings.

claim: 41.2% of the recorded neurons were lost as result of increased motor activity after anesthetic injection (14/34 neurons, 32 mice).
source: The injection was typically done after recording in baseline awake state for 4 min, and resulted in a significant increase in motor activity, with 41.2% of the recorded neurons lost as result of this (14/34 neurons, 32 mice).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation about recording loss due to motor activity.

claim: The increased time for pipette installation in the multipatcher is due to the increased complexity of tasks involved in positioning with close confinement.
source: The increased time for pipette installation is due to the increased complexity of tasks involved in positioning with close confinement.
evidence: This is an explanation for the observed difference in installation time.

claim: In the limit, scaling with this algorithm necessitates that operation time is 70 s/pipette (60 secs for gigasealing and 10 s for assessment).
source: In the limit, scaling with this algorithm necessitates that operation time is 70 s/pipette (60 secs for gigasealing and 10 s for assessment).
evidence: This is a calculation of the theoretical scaling limit based on the algorithm design.

claim: Practical limitations to pipette installation are 10–12 pipettes due to hardware constraints.
source: Using these methodologies, we estimate practical limitations to pipette installation are 10–12 pipettes due to hardware constraints, and the time for installation increases non-linearly.
evidence: This is an estimate of scaling limits based on hardware considerations.

claim: The time for installation increases non-linearly with the number of pipettes.
source: Using these methodologies, we estimate practical limitations to pipette installation are 10–12 pipettes due to hardware constraints, and the time for installation increases non-linearly.
evidence: This is an observation about scaling behavior.

claim: Whole-cell patch clamping is considered a gold standard electrophysiology tool.
source: Whole-cell patch clamping is considered a gold standard electrophysiology tool that enables the measurement of both suprathreshold spiking and subthreshold membrane potential fluctuations in single neurons.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the status of patch clamping in neuroscience.

claim: Whole-cell patch clamping enables the measurement of both suprathreshold spiking and subthreshold membrane potential fluctuations in single neurons.
source: Whole-cell patch clamping is considered a gold standard electrophysiology tool that enables the measurement of both suprathreshold spiking and subthreshold membrane potential fluctuations in single neurons.
evidence: This describes the capabilities of the technique based on established knowledge.

claim: The ability to whole-cell patch multiple neurons in brain slices has revealed key insights into the mechanisms of synaptic transmission and plasticity.
source: The ability to whole-cell patch multiple neurons in brain slices has revealed key insights into the mechanisms of synaptic transmission and plasticity (Perin et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Circuit level interrogations have been difficult to perform in vivo, particularly in awake animals.
source: Such circuit level interrogations have been difficult to perform in vivo, particularly in awake animals.
evidence: This is a statement about the challenges in the field based on the limited prior work.

claim: The automation of multi-neuron recording in vivo opens up the possibility of further parallelizing the multipatcher for high density mapping of the intracellular activity of ensembles of neurons in intact tissue.
source: The automation of multi-neuron recording in vivo opens up the possibility of further parallelizing the multipatcher for high density mapping of the intracellular activity of ensembles of neurons in intact tissue, which will be hard to accomplish by humans performing such tasks manually.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about future possibilities enabled by the technology.

claim: High density mapping of the intracellular activity of ensembles of neurons in intact tissue will be hard to accomplish by humans performing such tasks manually.
source: The automation of multi-neuron recording in vivo opens up the possibility of further parallelizing the multipatcher for high density mapping of the intracellular activity of ensembles of neurons in intact tissue, which will be hard to accomplish by humans performing such tasks manually.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of manual approaches.

claim: The advent of low-cost, silicon patch-chip amplifiers will enable scaling up the pipette count at a fraction of the cost compared to that of traditional analog amplifiers.
source: The advent of low-cost, silicon patch-chip amplifiers (Harrison et al., 2015) will enable scaling up the pipette count at a fraction of the cost compared to that of traditional analog amplifiers.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about future technological possibilities, citing relevant work.

claim: Imaging could be used for closed-loop control of multiple pipettes.
source: Imaging could be used for closed-loop control of multiple pipettes, as has already been done for single patch pipettes (Suk et al., 2017; Annecchino et al., 2017).
evidence: This is a suggestion for future development, supported by citations showing it has been done for single pipettes.

claim: Three or four fold increases in the number of simultaneously controlled pipettes could be achieved by using miniaturized micromanipulators and increasing the number of pneumatic valve banks.
source: Three or four fold increases in the number of simultaneously controlled pipettes could be achieved by using miniaturized micromanipulators, and increasing the number of pneumatic valve banks in the multipatcher control box—–both of which are possible using existing off-the-shelf hardware.
evidence: This is a prediction about future scaling possibilities based on available hardware.

claim: The macroscopic scale of currently used patch clamping pipettes will limit further increases in number of pipettes targeting the microcircuit.
source: The macroscopic scale of currently used patch clamping pipettes will limit further increases in number of pipettes targeting the microcircuit.
evidence: This is an inference about a fundamental limitation of the current approach.

claim: Novel electrode materials or microfabrication techniques that realize device architectures amenable for in vivo application will have to be developed to overcome pipette scaling limitations.
source: Thus, novel electrode materials, or microfabrication techniques that realize device architectures amenable for in vivo application will have to be developed.
evidence: This is a forward-looking statement about needed future developments.

claim: The time taken to assemble and position pipette arrays precisely at the brain surface will increase with the number of electrodes.
source: The time taken to assemble and position these pipette arrays precisely at the brain surface will also increase with the number of electrodes.
evidence: This is an inference about scaling behavior.

claim: Developing protocols to clean pipette tips for reuse will be particularly useful to overcome limitations in scaling.
source: Developing protocols to clean pipette tips for reuse (Kolb et al., 2016), improving the yield of regional pipette localization (Stoy et al., 2017), or incorporating hardware to robotically exchange pipettes between trials in dense pipette arrays, will be particularly useful to overcome this limitations.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future improvement, citing relevant work.

claim: Improving the yield of regional pipette localization will be particularly useful to overcome limitations in scaling.
source: Developing protocols to clean pipette tips for reuse (Kolb et al., 2016), improving the yield of regional pipette localization (Stoy et al., 2017), or incorporating hardware to robotically exchange pipettes between trials in dense pipette arrays, will be particularly useful to overcome this limitations.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future improvement, citing relevant work.

claim: Incorporating hardware to robotically exchange pipettes between trials in dense pipette arrays will be particularly useful to overcome limitations in scaling.
source: Developing protocols to clean pipette tips for reuse (Kolb et al., 2016), improving the yield of regional pipette localization (Stoy et al., 2017), or incorporating hardware to robotically exchange pipettes between trials in dense pipette arrays, will be particularly useful to overcome this limitations.
evidence: This is a suggestion for future improvement.

claim: Key skills for performing surgery, high quality durectomy, pulling pipettes, making internal solution, controlling pressure lines, etc., still remain a challenge and time and practice are required to master these skills.
source: However, the users that are less experienced in patch-clamp techniques should always keep in mind that key skills for performing surgery, high quality durectomy, pulling pipettes, making internal solution, controlling pressure lines, etc., still remain a challenge, and time and practice are required to master these skills (Kodandaramaiah et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a cautionary note about the technical requirements, citing prior work.

claim: All animal work was conducted in accordance to federal, state, and local regulations, and following NIH and AAALAC guidelines and standards.
source: We conducted all animal work in accordance to federal, state, and local regulations, and following NIH and AAALAC guidelines and standards.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical compliance.

claim: The corresponding protocol (#0113-008-16) was approved by the Institutional Committee on Animal Care at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
source: The corresponding protocol (#0113-008-16) was approved by the Institutional Committee on Animal Care at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology.
evidence: This is a statement about ethical approval.
